messages:
Maria (infra): heads-up — saw a spike of 429s and 95th latency climb in us-west-2 around 18:10 UTC. GPU pool at ~92% and queue depth spiked. Per-key token-bucket refill looks unchanged so heavy orgs starved others. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Ajay: yup, we've hit this when refill is static. If capacity drops, you end up with orgs holding steady refill but fewer slots -> overload. thinking: make refill proportional to available GPU slots or negotiated headroom.

Samir: proportial-refill makes sense. Also add short shared grace credits so small bursts don't immediately hit 429 for a noisy neighbor. grace credits could come from a lightweight global pool per-region.

Devon: quick question — do we want to modify token-bucket rates per-org, or switch to a leaky-bucket for ingress and keep token-buckets per-key downstream? Leaky at edge smooths arrivals; token-buckets still enforce accounting.

Maria (infra): good point. I'm worried about increased queuing latency if we push more into the queue. Some customer paths (low-latency) prefer immediate 429 over waiting 20s.

Ajay: agreed. idea: admission control with tiered responses — small queue (<2s expected) -> accept and queue, medium queue -> return 202 + advisory header with est wait, high -> 429. That keeps latency-sensitive clients failing fast.

Samir: operational details: we need a capacity signal from scheduler: available_gpu_slots(region) updated every 5s. Refill algorithm pseudocode: 
```
refill_rate_for_org = base_rate_for_org * (available_slots / total_slots)
refill_rate = max(refill_rate_for_org, min_rate)
```
Min_rate avoids starving low-volume orgs during outages.

Devon: also add model-fallback policy — if primary high-cost model is saturated, route to smaller quantized variant with a header showing model_fallback=true. That saves GPU capacity and prevents global penalty.

Maria (infra): do we have telemetry for org-level queued time? I can only see per-route latency and 429 counts atm. Need queue depth and avg wait per-org in Console.

OpsBot: alert: deploy 2164825000 finished to proxy-edge-us-west-2 :: release-candidate.

Ajay: might be related — new proxy changes to prefetch KV caches increased steady-state load. If proxy now batches more requests, GPUs see heavier concurrent KV working sets -> less throughput.

Samir: tradeoffs to consider:
- fairness vs throughput: proportional refill helps throughput but can let big orgs dominate if headroom calc is stale.
- complexity: regional shared grace pool + adaptive refill = operational load.
- cost: adding queueing/backpressure increases memory and autoscale triggers; could increase cost if we scale for peak queues.

Devon: can prototyping be isolated to a canary org + us-west-2? We can implement adaptive refill on a single proxy fleet and route a small percentage of keys. Config example for canary: 
```
admit:
  strategy: adaptive_refill
  region: us-west-2
  canary_percentage: 5
  min_rate_per_org: 1rps
  base_rates:
    free: 5rps
    standard: 50rps
    enterprise: 500rps
metrics:
  emit: [org_queue_depth, avg_wait_ms, refill_scaling_factor]
```

Maria (infra): +1 to canary. Action items: I will wire basic org_queue_depth metric into console (ETA today). Devon can you spin up the proxy canary with that config? Ajay, can you draft the refill algorithm and safety cutoffs (min_rate, max_scale) so we don't oscillate? Samir, propose grace-pool sizing rules.

Samir: will do. For grace pool sizing: start with 10% of total_slots as burst buffer, evaluate tail latency and adjust.

Ajay: draft ready — will post in this thread in ~30m with pseudocode and damping math (to avoid oscillation).

Devon: I'll open a PR and tag @Maria and @Ajay for review. Will route 5% traffic to canary and add fallback to 429/fast-fail.

Maria (infra): thanks all. if anyone sees another spike, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
